{"statements": {"L3.1": {"established": "partial", "quote": "When the players alternately select pieces of a fixed multiset \(L\), Liu Bang first, Liu Bang’s optimal total equals
\[
V(L)=\frac12\Bigl(\sum L+D(L)\Bigr).
\]
(The optimum is realised by always selecting a currently longest remaining piece.)", "note": "Correct alternating-sum reduction stated, but greedy optimality merely asserted, not proved."}, "L3.2": {"established": "no", "quote": null, "note": "Upper bound section is self-contradictory, abandons its own case analysis; no pigeonhole subset-sum or mirrored-cut construction for general n."}, "L3.3": {"established": "partial", "quote": "**Case \(k=0\).** Then \(Q=\{2^n\}\) and every element of \(P\) is at most \(2^{n-1}<2^n\). Hence the unique global maximum of \(M\) is \(2^n\) and
\[
D(M)=2^n-D(P).
\]
Since \(\sum P=2^n-1\) and \(D(P)\le\sum P\), one obtains \(D(M)\ge 2^n-(2^n-1)=1\).", "note": "Construction and Lemma A proved; induction only completes case k=0, k>=1 subcases garbled and lean on n<=3 numerics."}}, "S_ref": 0, "notes": "Correct answer and useful functional D with a genuine subadditivity/reverse-triangle lemma. Lower-bound induction breaks down for cuts inside the largest bin (placeholder text, appeals to numerical checks). Upper bound contains no valid argument at all, with visible corrupted text and an admitted contradiction. Neither obligation established."}
